question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Lose by a neck

options.text: To stop someone from putting forward his views

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Lose by a neck"** means to lose by a very small margin or difference. (बहुत कम अंतर से हारना)

 
 
• **Example:** In the horse race, he **lost by a neck**, finishing just inches behind the winner.
 
 
 
• **Lose by a small margin** refers to losing by a tiny amount or difference. (थोड़े से अंतर से हारना)
 
 
• **Example:** She **lost the election by a small margin** of just 50 votes.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the meaning of **'Lose by a neck'** is **'Lose by a small margin'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To lose one's necklace **(अपनी हार का हार खोना): This option does not relate to the idiom "Lose by a neck".

 
 
• **Example:** She was upset because she managed to lose her necklace at the party.
 
 
 
• **To stop someone from putting forward his views **(किसी को अपनी राय रखने से रोकना): This option does not convey the meaning of the idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** The moderator had to stop someone from putting forward his views as the time was up.
 
 
 
• **To cut short a matter** (मामले को संक्षिप्त करना): This option does not match the meaning of the idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** They decided to cut short the matter to avoid further complications.
 
 

3d:Tb46,
The correct answer is **Option 1.**
